# Frame TV Art Manager

> Frame TV Art Manager is a free, self-hosted service that keeps the Art Mode of one or more Samsung Frame TVs (The Frame) in sync with a folder of JPEG and PNG pictures on a NAS or home server. It prepares each picture for the TV's 3840x2160 screen, shows portraits and square art whole on a tinted charcoal gallery mat instead of cropping them, uploads over the local network, never uploads the same picture twice, and rotates art automatically when the TV's storage is full. No Samsung account, SmartThings account, or Art Store subscription is needed.

Last substantive update: 2026-11-06
Maintainer: MikeO7 (https://github.com/MikeO7)

## Key facts

- Who it is for: Samsung Frame TV owners with an always-on Synology, Unraid, or TrueNAS NAS, mini PC, Raspberry Pi-class Linux board, or Mac.
- Supported TVs: Samsung Frame TVs running Tizen 8.0 or newer. Other firmware may work, but Samsung's private Art Mode protocol varies between models and releases.
- Install: Docker image ghcr.io/mikeo7/frame-tv-art-manager:latest (amd64, arm64, armv7), or build a single Go binary.
- Only required setting: TV_IPS, a comma-separated list of TV IP addresses. Several TVs are supported from one collection.
- Storage: a persistent /data volume. Art lives in /data/artwork; pairing tokens and per-TV records live in /data/tokens.
- Pairing: on first connection the TV shows an Allow/Deny prompt named by CLIENT_NAME (default "Frame Art Manager"). Approve once.
- Schedule: first sync at startup, then every SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES (default 30).
- Connection: talks directly to the TV on the local network. It does not use SmartThings, its API, or any Samsung cloud service, and it does not touch the Samsung Art Store.
- Not a Home Assistant add-on; it runs as a separate container and exposes JSON status that Home Assistant can poll.

## Adding art

- Local folder of .jpg, .jpeg, and .png files. Pictures are identified by content hash, so the same picture is never uploaded twice, even after a rename.
- Optional web uploader: UPLOAD_ENABLED=true; HTTP Basic auth, username "frame", password UPLOAD_TOKEN (16+ characters); POST /upload on port 8080 with form field "file"; limit MAX_DOWNLOAD_SIZE_MB (default 20). Works from a browser, iPhone Shortcuts, and curl. HEIC is not accepted.
- Optional sources file (ARTWORK_SOURCES_FILE): NASA (APOD and search), Art Institute of Chicago (search and photo IDs), Unsplash, Pexels, Pixabay, and direct image URLs. The Art Institute search does not filter by public-domain status; use photo:<id> to pick public-domain works.

## Image preparation (on by default)

- EXIF orientation; ICC color profiles converted to sRGB; HDR PNGs tone-mapped; linear-light resize to exactly 3840x2160 (IMAGE_MAX_WIDTH, IMAGE_MAX_HEIGHT); halo-free contrast-adaptive sharpening, skipped for images enlarged more than 1.5x; JPEG quality 95 with full-resolution 4:4:4 chroma and optimized Huffman tables (IMAGE_JPEG_SUBSAMPLING=420 for smaller files); PNG stays PNG.
- Landscape pictures fill the screen only when cropping removes at most IMAGE_MAX_CROP_PERCENT (default 25) and enlargement is at most IMAGE_MAX_UPSCALE (default 3x). Otherwise they are shown whole.
- PORTRAIT_MODE: pad (default, shown whole), collage (two portraits paired by color, lightness, and shape in a double-opening mat; an unpaired one waits for a partner), or crop.
- IMAGE_PAD_STYLE: mat (default) is a deep charcoal gallery mat faintly tinted toward the art, with a lighter bevel, set slightly above center; a soft warm greige is used only when the art's edge is too dark. IMAGE_MAT_TONE=auto, dark, or light. blur fills the screen with a darkened blur instead.
- The prepared version replaces the original in the artwork folder, so users should copy pictures in and keep originals elsewhere.
- Optional and off by default: smart crop, an external crop service, and museum mode (canvas texture, warmth, smooth highlight roll-off).
- Samsung mattes: MATTE_STYLE (default none, for example shadowbox_polar), with per-file overrides in mattes.json.

## Full TVs and rotation

- The manager learns a TV's capacity the first time the TV rejects an upload because storage is full.
- If the collection is larger, each piece the manager uploaded stays at least ROTATION_INTERVAL_DAYS (default 14; 0 disables), then is swapped for waiting art: never-shown pieces first, then the pieces away longest.
- Each swap is one delete followed immediately by one upload. Only the manager's own uploads rotate. Local files are never deleted.
- /status shows rotating, artwork_waiting, and next_rotation for each TV.

## Safety rules

- Never deletes TV art it did not upload unless REMOVE_UNKNOWN_IMAGES=true.
- Does not choose which artwork is displayed.
- Keeps the last piece it uploaded if the folder becomes empty.
- A failed source download never deletes previously downloaded art.
- Makes no changes to a TV whose state it cannot confirm.
- DRY_RUN=true plans without uploading, deleting, saving state, or waking the TV.

## Optional TV controls

- Slideshow: SLIDESHOW_ENABLED, SLIDESHOW_INTERVAL (3, 15, 60, 720, or 1440 minutes), SLIDESHOW_TYPE (shuffle or sequential).
- Brightness: fixed BRIGHTNESS (0-50), or SOLAR_BRIGHTNESS_ENABLED with latitude, longitude, and timezone.
- Nightly power-off for TVs in Art Mode: AUTO_OFF_TIME.
- Wake-on-LAN: TV_MAC, sent only when the TV is confirmed off; single TV only.

## Planned, not available yet

- A built-in MCP server so AI assistants can curate themed art sets and send them to the TV without API keys.

## Common questions

- Does it need a Samsung Art Store subscription? No.
- Does it need a Samsung or SmartThings account? No.
- Will it delete art I added myself? No, unless REMOVE_UNKNOWN_IMAGES=true.
- Will it crop portrait photos? Not by default; they are shown whole on a gallery mat.
- What size is the output? 3840x2160, 16:9, sRGB.
- What happens when the TV is full? It rotates the art it uploaded, 14 days per piece by default.
- Is it open source? No. It is source-available under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 and free for noncommercial use.
